angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 930,847 km at 462.41 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 2.1626 +/- 0.0140 mas (same row, RUWE 1.07): 462.41 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.338 +/- 0.065 solar radii from Wang et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HAT-P-9 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157...82W/abstract): 930,847 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.281 +/- 0.057 solar masses from Wang et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HAT-P-9 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157...82W/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6350 +/- 150 K from Wang et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-9 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157...82W/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Wang et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-9 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157...82W/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hat-p-9.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.293, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
